explanation: The Romans called it Quintilis, the fifth month, because their year once began in March. It was renamed in Caesar's honour in 44 BC, the year of his death, and August later honoured Augustus.

The month was renamed in Caesar's honour in 44 BC, the year of his death.

issues.note: Checker doubt on x1. The explanation says July 'was renamed for Caesar after his death in 44 BC'. To my knowledge the renaming was decreed among the honours voted to Caesar while he was alive, and the name first applied to July 44 BC, after his death, so 'after his death' is misleading at best. c4 already has a safe form: 'in 44 BC, the year of his death'. Suggested explanation: 'It was renamed in Caesar's honour in 44 BC, the year he was killed, and August later honoured Augustus.'
